The picture shown when you share a link is your site's **og:image**. You can set it for a single page or for the whole site, and the change only goes live after you **publish**.

**For one page:**
1. In the Editor, click **Pages & Menu** on the left.
2. Click the page, then **More Actions** → **Social share**.
3. Click **Upload Image**, choose or upload an image, and click **Add to Page**.
4. **Publish your site.**

**For the whole site:**
1. Open your site's settings and click **Website settings**.
2. Scroll to **General social image** and click **Upload Image**.
3. Choose the image, click **Choose File**, then **Save** at the top of the dashboard.
4. **Publish your site.**

A few things that often explain why it didn't change:
- If a page has its own og:image, that one is used for that page. The site-wide image is only used for pages without one.
- The image should have a **1.91:1** aspect ratio (width about 1.9 × the height) to avoid cropping.
- If your SEO settings use an image variable or image URL for og:image (under **Basics & social share**), that setting controls the image too.

Sorry about the denied documents. For a **business account**, company details are usually rejected because something doesn't match exactly. Please check:

**Company information**
- Your company's name and its registration number / tax ID must match the company's registered information.
- The **Legal Business Name, Shareholder and VAT ID / Business ID / Tax ID / EIN** in the form must match those on your **business bank account**.
- Upload a document that proves the validity and ownership of that VAT ID / Business ID / Tax ID / EIN.

**Document requirements (e.g. an EIN confirmation)**
- The company name and the number must be clearly visible and match your Wix Payments business details.
- Formats: jpeg, jpg, pdf or png. Max 10 MB; min 1 kB for PDF, 100 kB for other formats.

**Bank documents are rejected if they:**
- are blurry, too small to read, torn, rotated or a mobile screenshot
- don't show the full account number, or the name/company doesn't match your account
- are a direct deposit form instead of a bank statement

Also make sure your address document is from the last 6 months (bank letters: last 12 months) and that you used a physical address, not a PO Box.

After re-submitting, allow **7 business days**. If that passes and everything matches your bank details, contact Wix Customer Care to investigate.

A gap at the bottom of the live page usually comes from the page being longer than its content. Two fixes in the Wix Editor:

**Gap between your content and the footer**
- Shorten the page: click and drag the **Adjust Page Height** icon so the page ends where your content ends.
- If your page is covered in strips, click and pull the footer down first so you can click the main part of the page.

**Gap below the footer on the live site**
This appears when the page content is shorter than the page length. You can:
1. **Change the page background color** to match your footer, so the gap looks like part of the footer.
2. **Add content** to the page so it covers most of the screen (on very large screens a small gap can still show).
3. **Resize the footer** to make it longer.

Note there's always a gap below the footer inside the Editor itself; that one is there so you can resize the footer and doesn't mean anything is wrong.

Yes. Your Premium plan stays on your site; you just connect the new domain to it and it replaces the current one. Your plan must still be **active**.

**1. Add the new domain to your Wix account first**, using one of these:
- Connect a domain purchased elsewhere to Wix
- Transfer a domain to Wix
- (or purchase one from Wix)

**2. Assign it to your site:**
1. Go to **Domains** in your Wix account.
2. Click **Assign** next to *Not Assigned to a Site* (scroll to the right domain if you have several).
3. Select your site and click **Next**.
4. Because the site is already connected to your old domain, choose:
   - **Replace the current primary domain** – connects the new domain and disconnects the old one, or
   - **Redirect it to the primary domain** – keeps the old one as primary and redirects.
5. Click **Assign**.

If the domain was purchased elsewhere, also make sure the correct A record and CNAME records are added in your domain host's account.

To delete a Wix site, you move it to the Trash:

1. Go to the site's **dashboard**.
2. Click the **Site Actions** icon at the top of the page.
3. Click **Move to Trash**.
4. Click **Move to Trash** again to confirm.

Before you do this, **cancel any premium services** on the site (site plan, domain, subscriptions); deleting the site doesn't cancel them. Once they're canceled, you can keep your Wix account open for free.

If you only want the site offline but not deleted, you can unpublish it instead. And if you want to remove everything, you can close your whole account after moving all sites to Trash and canceling all services.

Yes. Your **Booking Calendar** shows what's already booked alongside the free slots, so you can see taken times before booking or rescheduling:

- **Weekly view:** your whole week, including all sessions and free time slots.
- **Daily view:** the selected date, including all free time slots.
- **Staff view:** upcoming sessions for a date, in columns per staff member.
- **Schedule:** a list of the day's sessions with time, type, participants, staff and location.

If you're rescheduling an appointment in the Wix app, you can also tap **Show free time slots** while editing it to see the staff member's other available times and pick a new one.

You can remove a saved card from the **Payment Methods** page in your Wix account:

1. Go to **Payment Methods** in your Wix account.
2. Click **Actions** next to the card.
3. Click **Remove**, then **Remove** again to confirm.

**Important:** you can only remove a payment method that isn't connected to an **active subscription** (e.g. a site plan, domain or business email). If the card is still in use, first switch those subscriptions to another payment method (Payment Methods → Actions → Update), or cancel them.

Once removed, nobody with billing permissions on your account can use that card for future purchases.

The help articles don't explain this exact situation, but they point to a few common reasons a form submitter isn't (or isn't yet) listed as subscribed:

- **Only subscribe forms subscribe people automatically.** People who fill out a *subscribe form* are added to your contacts with a **Subscriber** label. Other forms only subscribe someone if the form includes a **subscribe to mailing list** field and they opt in.
- **Double opt-in:** if **Enable double opt-in** is on, subscribers must verify their email before they're subscribed. Anyone who hasn't clicked the confirmation won't show as subscribed yet.
- **Require consent:** if your subscribe element requires consent, people must tick the consent checkbox to be subscribed.

You can check someone's status on their contact card; subscribed contacts show a **SUBSCRIBED** label. If none of these explains what you're seeing, I can connect you with a member of our support team to look at the specific contacts.

I want to make sure I point you to the right setting. Which search do you mean?

**1. How your page appears in Google search results** (the title vs. the description under it):
- Edit them per page: **Pages & Menu** → **More Actions** next to the page → **SEO basics** → edit the **Title tag** (and meta description), then **publish**.
- Search engines need to recrawl your site before changes show, and they may sometimes choose other text from your page if they think it fits better.

**2. The search box on your own site** (Wix Site Search):
- Click the search box in the Editor → **Settings** to change the placeholder text, and use **Layout** and **Design** to change its look.
- On the **Search Results** page settings you can choose which types of results to show.

The articles I have don't cover making the site search box search descriptions instead of titles. If that's what you need, I can connect you with a member of our support team.
